translation:
  text: '“The believers from the third mountain, which had thorns and briars, are like this: some are
    rich, and others are entangled in many business affairs. The briars are the rich; the thorns are those
    entangled in various business affairs.”


    2. “These people, then, who are entangled in many different business affairs, do not[a] attach themselves
    to God’s servants. Instead, they wander away, choked by their activities. The rich find it hard to
    attach themselves to God’s servants, fearing that something may be demanded of them.[b] Such people
    will therefore enter God’s kingdom only with difficulty.”


    3. “For just as it is difficult to walk barefoot among briars, it is difficult for such people to
    enter God’s kingdom.”


    4. “But repentance is available to all these people, and it must be swift,[c] so that they may now
    make up the days and do some good that they did not do before. If, then, they repent and do some good,[d]
    they will live to God. But if they persist in their activities, they will be handed over to those
    women, who will put them to death.[e]”'
  philosophy: optimal-equivalence
  footnotes:
  - marker: a
    reason: textual_variant
    text: The printed source supplies the preceding description and “not” in brackets, following Gebhardt’s
      insertion compared with the two Latin traditions and Ethiopic. Athos is reported to omit the bracketed
      span; without “not,” it reads “These people attach themselves to God’s servants, but wander away.”
      This draft provisionally retains the supplied negation. P.Oxy.3528’s surviving fragment does not
      cover this clause.
  - marker: b
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: The fear is rendered as a demand or request being made of the rich, in the context of their
      reluctance to associate with God’s servants. The source does not specify a donation, a sum, or a
      named recipient.
  - marker: c
    reason: textual_variant
    text: The printed text has an unusual swift-repentance adjective and a “make up the days” expression.
      The apparatus reports Athos with an additional “in” before “the days”; this draft retains the printed
      construction. The difficult wording is not converted into a precise deadline.
  - marker: d
    reason: textual_variant
    text: '“If, then, they repent and do some good” is an editorial insertion marked by vertical bars
      in the working edition, attributed to Hilgenfeld and compared with Latin Vulgata/Palatina; Athos
      is reported to have “and” instead. Without the inserted condition: “But repentance is available
      to all these people, and it must be swift, so that they may now make up the days and do some good
      that they did not do before, and they will live to God.” Oxford’s P.Oxy.3528 image preserves only
      a small overlap around paragraphs3–4, not the complete inserted condition.'
  - marker: e
    reason: textual_variant
    text: '“Women” follows Anger’s printed conjecture compared with the Latin traditions and Ethiopic;
      Athos is reported as “activities.” Alternative: “They will be handed over to those activities, which
      will put them to death.” The women are figures in the vision, not women as a general class.'
